verbalization: Ketoprofen exhibits a mechanistic link to Solute carrier organic anion transporter family member 1B1 through a multi-step pathway. The evidence suggests that Ketoprofen targets P-glycoprotein 1, a member of the ATP-binding cassette (ABC) transporter family, which is known to facilitate the efflux of various substrates from cells. This efflux activity is further modulated by (3R,5S,7S)-8-hydroxy-4,4,7-trimethyl-9-(2-methylbutanoyl)-3-prop-1-en-2-yltricyclo[5.3.1.01,5]undec-8-ene-10,11-dione, a complex organic compound that acts as a target of P-glycoprotein 1. The final step in this pathway involves the transporter Solute carrier organic anion transporter family member 1B1, which is responsible for the transport of organic anions across cellular membranes. The cumulative evidence supports a mechanism where Ketoprofen indirectly influences Solute carrier organic anion transporter family member 1B1 through the modulation of P-glycoprotein 1, highlighting a potential role in drug resistance or transport-related physiological processes.
